title: Current public full-clip decoder comparison: goav1 vs installed dav1d

source_identity.corpus_ivf_sha256_manifest: per-clip IVF SHA-256s are embedded in the raw timing records
source_identity.go_build_source_state: At test-binary build time, HEAD was ff35737478053df7c9ed6c4c9aa06ad626820d57 and the only worktree modification was internal/av1/motion/subpel_probe_test.go. The overlay restored that test file to HEAD. Production sources matched HEAD at build time. Subsequent candidate source edits occurred after the immutable benchmark binary was frozen and cannot affect these timing runs.

corpus_and_boundary.go_timed_operation: NewDecoderFromIVF(preloaded IVF bytes) + all DecodeNext calls + touch first/last visible byte of Y/U/V and dimensions + Close; constructor parses IVF and copies packet payloads
corpus_and_boundary.dav1d_timed_operation: parse IVF records from preloaded whole-file bytes + fresh single-thread dav1d context + wrap packet slices (no payload copy) + submit/drain/observe first/last visible byte of each Y/U/V plane + unref pictures + close
corpus_and_boundary.excluded_from_both: file reads, input SHA-256, sidecar reads, full-output MD5 preflight and result comparison; process startup
corpus_and_boundary.output_correctness: all 18 clips matched independent stream-MD5 sidecars in both Go constructors and the C helper before timing in each run; Go and C preflight MD5s agree clip by clip.
corpus_and_boundary.boundary_difference: Go NewDecoderFromIVF copies packet payloads during its timed constructor; dav1d wraps preloaded slices. C still parses IVF frame records in the timed interval. This is a public-API comparison, not an isolated language/SIMD comparison.
corpus_and_boundary.sampling_protocol: two serialized full-corpus rounds with backend order Go then dav1d, then dav1d then Go; each backend/clip has one warmup per round and nine raw timed samples per round (two warmups and 18 samples total)
corpus_and_boundary.statistics: round samples are clustered by run, not randomized matched pairs. Combined per-clip median is the mean of the two middle values from the 18 samples; aggregate is the sum of per-clip medians. Reversing order reveals but does not eliminate drift; no paired-significance claim.
corpus_and_boundary.shared_workstation_note: builds and timing runs were serialized; no CPU affinity or frequency controls were applied.
corpus_and_boundary.secondary_go_paths: cold NewDecoder(payloads) medians exclude IVF parsing and packet copy before timing; warm Reset+DecodeNext reuses one decoder. Their raw samples and per-clip medians are included but they have no matched dav1d comparison and are excluded from the primary ratio.
corpus_and_boundary.historical_results_note: This is a new 2026-10-17 snapshot on lifecycle-fixed commit ff357374; do not pool or directly compare with the dated 2026-10-09 table, which used a different Go checkpoint and a statically built dav1d.
